issues.claim: The overview of common web application architectures also describes an "all-in-one" application with a single project as the simplest starting structure, and clean architecture as an approach that puts the business logic and application model at the center.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt is only the tail of the page and does not show this wording. It matches the page's 'All-in-one applications' and 'Clean architecture' sections as I know them: the simplest architecture keeps all concerns in one project, and clean architecture puts business logic and application model at the center. The claim is correct, but the excerpt cannot confirm it. The core claim is anyway fully supported by the DDD-oriented microservice excerpt.
issues.suggestedFix: No change required. The owner may optionally name the page sections ('All-in-one applications', 'Clean architecture') when re-verifying.

issues.claim: A service owned by two teams grows an implicit internal boundary, conflicts and constant coordination ... The result is a distributed monolith.
issues.problem: These two symptoms are standard architectural practice, but they are not stated on the cited Fowler pages, which cover layer-oriented teams, location and time zones, and small teams producing a monolith. They are presented as the answer's own reasoning, not as claims attributed to Fowler, so this is acceptable.
issues.suggestedFix: No change required. Optionally do not attribute these bullets to Fowler.
